title: Deepak Jain v. State of U.P. & Others
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J. & Prashant Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of; connection application to be decided in four weeks
headnote: Electricity supply, monopolised by the U.P. Power Corporation, is essential for life. A tenant/occupier cannot be refused an electricity connection merely for want of the landlord's consent. Following the Division Bench in Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd., the application of a tenant is to be considered under Clause 4.4 read with Annexures 4.2 and 4.3 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which provide either for a consent letter of the owner or, in its absence, an Indemnity Bond furnished by the lessee/tenant/occupier. The Court directed the competent authority to decide the tenant's pending application within four weeks after hearing the parties with a stake.

holding_units.topic: Tenant's connection: owner's consent letter OR indemnity bond
holding_units.question: Can a tenant be refused a connection for want of the landlord's consent?
holding_units.holding: No. A lessee/tenant/occupier cannot be refused a connection merely for want of the landlord's consent; under Clause 4.4 read with Annexures 4.2 and 4.3, the application is considered either on a consent letter of the owner or, in its absence, on an Indemnity Bond furnished by the tenant. The competent authority must decide the tenant's application within four weeks after hearing the stakeholders.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Tenant of a first-floor portion; application allotted a service number and inspection done, but connection not provided.

principle_tags.application: A tenant/occupier is entitled to a connection under Clause 4.4 on the owner's consent letter or, absent it, an Indemnity Bond (Annexures 4.2/4.3); want of the landlord's consent is no ground to refuse.

lead_authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.

authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
authorities.citation: Writ - C No. 28295 of 2014 (Allahabad HC, Division Bench)
authorities.proposition: An application for a connection cannot be refused for want of the landlord's consent; on furnishing an indemnity bond, a lessee/tenant/occupier cannot be refused a connection merely for want of consent of the landlord.
authorities.how_treated: Followed as the governing Division Bench authority.
